reviews.one_line_contribution: On ALFWorld, hold the reader and the bank fixed and vary the action-level noise (detours) of the stored trajectories at several levels, then show that top-k retrieval transmits the rank-1 item's detours into the episode while a whole-bank many-shot prefix is insensitive to the bank's detour rate — with a detour-pruning arm and a token-matched sham-prune to prove the effect is detour content, not item length.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two verified papers split the claim between them. (1) arxiv:2405.00200 (Bertsch et al., NAACL, verified via s2cli `paper`, 157 cites): long-context ICL gains do not come from cumulative encoding, and retrieval's advantage over unselected demonstrations is large at small shot counts and shrinks as the shot count grows — which is P2/P3 (whole-bank catches up, retrieval's selection advantage evaporates) already stated at the mechanism level, on classification. (2) arxiv:2412.16926 (ACL, verified via s2cli; TLDR returned by search: "Long Context Language Models reduce the sensitivity of In-Context Learning to example selection techniques and instead emphasize the importance of sufficient and augmented examples") — that is, in the many-shot regime what you select matters less, which is the proposal's whole-bank-is-robust half. arxiv:2411.07130 (MANYICLBENCH, verified via search listing) even names the two reading modes as 'similar-sample learning' vs 'all-sample learning'. On the agent side, arxiv:2512.16962 (MemoryGraft, verified, 59 cites) established the 'semantic imitation heuristic' — agents copy the retrieved item — and arxiv:2607.10608 (compliance trap, verified) traced when a wrong retrieved memory enters and propagates through a trajectory. What is genuinely new is narrow but real: noise that lives in the action sequence rather than the label, set at several levels by construction (S / A / P / Sh), and the read route crossed with it. The proposal's framing of 2405.00200 as predicting the *opposite* (whole-bank inherits the nearest item) is a selective read: the same paper's retrieval-advantage-shrinks result predicts the proposal's own headline, so 2405.00200 is better described as a partial scoop of P2/P3 in another domain than as the competitor hypothesis.
reviews.strongest_objection: There is no positive control for the whole-bank route, so its predicted insensitivity is not distinguishable from its reading little of the bank at all. Every retrieval arm has one (RET A, matched on type and expert length, differing only in detour steps), but nothing in the design shows that a WB48 prefix is sensitive to *any* property of the bank it was drawn from. If whole-bank reading on a six-template environment simply recovers the type's procedure from whatever is in front of it — which is what this node has already measured (unseen ≈ seen; static3 alone is +12.4 over k0; instr_all, six hand-written procedures, is +9.5 over k0) — then WB48 S ≈ WB48 E is entailed by the route being near-static, not by any averaging over noisy items, and P2's +9 interaction is carried almost entirely by RET S falling (the P1–P2 shared-term problem the entailment check flags). The paper's title claim, 'averages out', is exactly the part the design cannot confirm: P6 is an equivalence test on the whole-bank slope with no stated MDE, a bound b defined as half the *observed* retrieval slope (so it loosens whenever the retrieval effect is large), a bank-mean regressor taking 16 distinct values, an 'else underpowered' escape clause, and the only positive consensus signature (modal-wrong-receptacle share) declared exploratory. P3, the dose that would show the whole-bank route uses item count at all, is by the proposal's own arithmetic below its noise floor (WB contrasts ~11 net at two seeds against an 8–9 decision boundary) and is explicitly excluded from the seed extension. So the two predictions that carry the mechanism are underpowered by the proposal's own numbers, and what survives at power is 'retrieval passes detours' (P1/P5/P7) — a trajectory-level confirmation of MemoryGraft's imitation heuristic — plus a null on a route that may not be reading the bank.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Add a whole-bank placebo ladder that establishes the route reads its items before any robustness null is interpreted: WB48 built entirely from wrong-type items (the WB counterpart of blind1), and WB48 built from *failed* or action-corrupted trajectories (actions shuffled within item, or receptacle names permuted). If WB48-wrong-type and WB48-corrupt sit at the same success as WB48 E and WB48 S, the whole-bank arm is a static prompt with extra tokens and P2/P6 are uninterpretable; if they drop, the insensitivity to detour rate becomes a real robustness result with a measured dynamic range. Second, pre-register an absolute equivalence bound b for P6 from measured SDs rather than half the observed retrieval slope, and raise bank draws (more than 8 per arm-seed) until the equivalence CI can actually fit inside b; the same applies to the P3 dose contrast, which must enter the blinded seed-extension rule instead of being frozen at two seeds. Third, decouple P7: run M1 with one self item at rank 1 versus a one-self-item-at-rank-3 arm so rank is not confounded with detoured-item count, and match A's bank size to S's by subsampling S so the positive control does not also vary retrieval similarity. Fourth, since success is at 0.87 ceiling, promote steps and step-limit failures to co-primary rather than fallback.
reviews.missing_baseline: A whole-bank content placebo — WB48 of wrong-type items and/or WB48 of corrupted or failed trajectories, matched in item count and tokens. Without it, 'the whole-bank route is insensitive to the detour rate' has no upper bound on what the route *is* sensitive to, and a reviewer reads the P2/P6 nulls as the route ignoring its bank. A close second: a token-matched cached static arm at WB48 length (e.g. the six-procedure instr_all padded to ~13k tokens, already measured at +9.5 over k0), so the whole-bank cell is scored against 'a long cached prefix' and not only against retrieval.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. Queries I ran, all through the s2cli channel (Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace, both channels reported ok on every call); WebSearch unavailable in this session, WebFetch never used. (1) 'whole context versus retrieval top-k demonstrations robustness to noisy demonstrations many-shot aggregation' — returned arxiv:2405.00200, 2411.07130, 2503.08640, 2506.04579, 2202.12837, 2502.16101 (RAGuard, misleading retrievals in RAG); nothing on trajectory banks. (2) 'agent experience memory suboptimal self-generated trajectories detours imitation retrieval versus full context' --recent — returned arxiv:2607.28272 (MemHarness: retrieved experience reconstructed rather than replayed, negative transfer), 2607.10608, 2606.19911 (Multi-Agent Transactive Memory), 2604.27003 (experience reuse as a retrieval-level continual-learning problem), 2605.12493 (LongMemEval-V2, AgentRunbook-R vs -C); none sets a noise rate on the bank or crosses read route with it. (3) 'increasing number of shots dilutes label noise many-shot in-context learning robust to incorrect demonstrations' — returned arxiv:2411.19581, 2404.11018, 1705.10694; label noise in classification only. (4) 'retrieval advantage diminishes with more demonstrations long-context ICL example selection sensitivity' — arxiv:2405.00200, 2411.07130, 2605.13511 (Many-Shot CoT-ICL: ordering and selection still matter for reasoning tasks — a counterweight the proposal does not cite), 2408.13987 (FocusICL: many-shot degraded by unimportant content). (5) 'long context language models in-context learning example selection random sampling noise sensitivity revisiting' — arxiv:2412.16926, the nearest threat (see closest_prior_work). (6) 'long context versus retrieval agent memory bank all experiences in prompt top-k comparison' --recent — arxiv:2608.15008 (Harness the Memory: holistic evaluation of memory substrates, regime-dependent trade-offs) and 2602.02007; substrate-level, no per-item noise manipulation. (7) 'suboptimal demonstrations in context degrade LLM agent decision making' --recent — nothing on point. IDs verified with s2cli `paper`: 2405.00200 (NAACL, 157 cites), 2404.11018 (NeurIPS, 264), 2412.16926 (ACL, 12), 2411.19581, 2605.24117 (SkillEvolBench), 2605.29463 (Honest Lying), 2512.16962 (MemoryGraft, 59), 2607.10608 (compliance trap) — all resolve as described. 2411.07130 resolved through search listings rather than the `paper` call. The proposal's own Preprint Collision Check is above average for this pipeline: four classed queries, IDs listed, channels named, WebSearch honestly reported as unavailable. Its defect is not thinness but framing — it presents arxiv:2405.00200 only as the competitor that predicts copying and does not report that the same paper's retrieval-advantage-shrinks-with-shots finding, together with arxiv:2412.16926's verified 'LCLMs reduce sensitivity to example selection', already states the proposal's headline direction in the classification setting. Novelty should be scored as domain transfer plus one new manipulation (detour rate, prune vs sham-prune), not as a new mechanism.
